fields.meta_title: NPS Survey Builder That Does the Math | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an NPS survey that asks the 0-10 question, works out your score, splits it by plan, and emails you when a low score comes in.
fields.h1: Build an NPS Survey That Works Out Your Score
fields.hero_description: Get an NPS survey that asks the 0-10 question, calculates your score, and saves every answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: One Question and What Follows From It
fields.features_subheading: Customers see only the first feature. The other five score each answer and get it to the person who can act on it.
fields.feature_1:
The 0-10 question and a reason box

Emergent writes the recommend question on a 0-10 scale, then an open box asking what drove the score. On a phone, each of the two questions gets a full screen of its own.
fields.feature_2:
The score, with each group counted

The dashboard sorts every answer into promoter, passive, or detractor and shows the score next to the share in each group. When the score changes, you can see which group moved.
fields.feature_3:
An email when a score of 6 or below lands

Pick who hears about low scores, and the app emails that person the score and the comment, with the customer's name on top. Teams that work in Slack can get it in a channel there.
fields.feature_4:
Results split by plan or location

Add a field for the plan, product, or location, and the dashboard works out a separate score for each value. A company-wide score can hide one plan that sits far below all the rest.
fields.feature_5:
Sent after the event that matters

Connect your billing system or CRM by API, and the app can send the survey when a record changes, such as a renewal. Each answer can sync back to that customer's record.
fields.feature_6:
Your survey's code, exported to GitHub

On paid plans, Emergent exports the full survey app to your GitHub repository, with the scoring logic and the dashboard. From there, the code is yours to read or extend.

fields.tab_content_1:
Kestrel Yoga lands on 30 after the 10th class

Kestrel Yoga sends the survey to each member the day after their 10th class. Of 400 answers, 200 come from promoters and 80 from detractors, and the dashboard shows a score of 30. The other 120 are passives, and several of them ask for more evening classes.
fields.tab_content_2:
Low on Starter, high on Team

Ledgerly sells three plans and splits its NPS by plan. Team scores 55 on 100 answers and Pro scores 38 on 200, but Starter sits at 12 on 150 answers. The product team opens the Starter comments first, where bank import is the top complaint.
fields.tab_content_3:
A 4 from a cleaning customer reaches Odalys by email

Saltmarsh Home Cleaning customer Teodor Vance scores his visit a 4 and writes that the upstairs bathroom was missed. Operations manager Odalys Ferreira gets an email with his score and note, and she books a return visit for Friday.
fields.tab_content_4:
In Q3 the tenant score reaches 27

Alderbrook Property Management asks its tenants the same two questions every quarter. The score was 12 in Q1 and 19 in Q2. In Q3 it reaches 27 on 318 answers, with 140 promoters and 54 detractors, and slow repairs drop out of the top comments.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an NPS Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build an NPS survey with Emergent, send it at a moment that matters, and follow up on every low score.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the moment that sends it
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Save the field you will split by
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide which moment sends the survey before you write a word: the day after a 10th class, or the first week of each quarter. Give each moment its own survey. A score taken after one event should never be averaged with a score taken after another.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Tell Emergent who answers, when the survey goes out, and what the dashboard should show. Emergent builds the survey and its database from that prompt, with the scoring on the dashboard. To change anything later, ask for it in a sentence.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask the recommend question as the Net Promoter System words it, "How likely are you to recommend us to a friend or colleague?", on a 0-10 scale. Put the name customers know you by in place of "us", and add the reason box as the second and last question.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Carry the plan or location into each answer from your own records, instead of asking the customer to type it. One clean field is what lets the dashboard show a separate score for each group.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Name who hears about low scores
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose one person for each team or location to hear about every detractor. Name a person rather than a shared inbox, so each reply has an owner and nobody waits on a message that everyone assumed someone else had read.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Answer the survey yourself on a phone and on a laptop, then send it to 10 customers you know well. Check that a 9, a 7, and a 3 each land in the right group on the dashboard before the full send.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Open the dashboard after the first week and read the comments next to the score. Reply to each detractor within 2 days, and tell customers what you changed because of what they wrote.

faq_plan.q: What is a good NPS survey score?
faq_plan.ref: What is a good NPS survey score?

prov.original: What is a good NPS survey score?

faq_plan.a: Any score above 0 is good. Qualtrics reports that Bain & Company, which created NPS, suggests above 0 is good, above 20 is favorable, and above 50 is excellent, with a top band above 80. The score is a number from -100 to +100. Hold your own result against last quarter's too, since a rise from 12 to 19 says more about your progress than either number does alone.

faq_plan.q: How do you create an NPS survey?
faq_plan.ref: how to create an nps survey
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI survey builder: who answers, when it goes out, and what you want to see on the dashboard. Emergent builds the 0-10 question and the reason box from that prompt, along with the score calculation, and changes any of it when you ask in a sentence. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: When should you send an NPS survey after a purchase?
faq_plan.a: Send it once the customer has used what they bought, not at checkout. For a physical product, wait a few days after delivery. For software, wait about 30 days after signup, when the first real use is behind them. Ask at checkout only when the buying process itself is what you want scored.

faq_plan.q: How often should you send an NPS survey?
faq_plan.ref: how often to send nps survey
faq_plan.a: Send a relationship NPS survey once a quarter, which gives you 4 scores a year to compare. For open comments between those rounds, run a customer feedback survey alongside it, with its own questions. Whatever the rhythm, never send the relationship survey to the same customer more than once in 90 days.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should an NPS survey have?
faq_plan.ref: how many questions in nps survey
faq_plan.a: Two: the 0-10 recommend question and one open question asking for the reason behind the score. Add a third only when a decision depends on its answer, and make it a pick list that takes one tap. Every answer, however short the survey, saves to the same database row as the score.

faq_plan.q: What is an NPS survey used for?
faq_plan.ref: what is nps survey used for
faq_plan.a: An NPS survey measures how likely customers are to recommend you, on a zero-to-ten scale. The score is the percentage of promoters, who scored 9 or 10, minus the percentage of detractors, who scored 0 to 6. The Net Promoter System site says the score can be tracked for a whole company and also for each business, product, store, or customer-service team.

faq_plan.q: How do you automate NPS surveys and customer feedback?
faq_plan.ref: how to automate nps surveys customer feedback
faq_plan.a: Write the trigger into your prompt as a rule, such as 30 days after the first paid invoice, and connect the app to the tool that holds that date. The same app can send a customer effort score question each time a support ticket closes, on a trigger of its own. A survey built on Emergent has no response cap, so every customer can get one.

faq_plan.q: When in the customer lifecycle should you send out an NPS survey?
faq_plan.ref: when to send out nps survey
faq_plan.a: Send it out at points where the customer has a view of the whole relationship: after onboarding ends, a month before renewal, and each quarter for long-term accounts. After a single visit or ticket, ask about that one interaction and keep the answer out of the relationship score. Skip the week of an outage: one bad day should not stand in for the whole relationship.

faq_plan.q: What should NPS survey software track for each answer?
faq_plan.a: It should track each score with its comment and the customer it came from. It should also chart the score and alert a named person when a detractor answers. In the app Emergent builds, answers sit in a database you own that you can filter or connect by API to the tools you already use.

faq_plan.q: Is there an NPS survey template to start from?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Pick one of the NPS prompt chips at the top of this page, or start from the default prompt and add what you need, such as a plan field or a quarterly trend. To score several touchpoints instead of the recommend question alone, start from a customer experience survey and add the 0-10 question to it as the first item.

plan.angle: The top 10 explains what NPS is and how to calculate it, with a few template slots; none builds the survey that does the arithmetic and acts on it. This page is for the team that runs the survey: the 0-10 question and a reason box, the score worked out on the dashboard, results split by plan, an email to the right person when a low score lands, and quarter-by-quarter trends, with every answer a row in a database the team owns. The FAQ handles timing, frequency, length and the formula as plain advice, with the formula sourced to the Net Promoter System site.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build an NPS Survey That Works Out Your Score'; hero 'Get an NPS survey that asks the 0-10 question, calculates your score, and saves every answer to a database you own.'; howto_description one sentence.

intent.evidence: Top 10 cover definition, calculation, good score, best practices, questions; page has the formula (FAQ 6), good-score bands (FAQ 1), standard question (step 3), timing and cadence (FAQ 3, 4, 8), plus a builder angle.

specificity.evidence: NPS vocabulary throughout: promoters, passives, detractors, relationship NPS, score by plan, 'a 9, a 7, and a 3 each land in the right group'.

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on full sentences: 'Kestrel Yoga sends the survey...', 'Ledgerly sells three plans...', 'Pick who hears about low scores...'.

craft.evidence: One idea per sentence; QC Q5 2 ', so' endings (step 5, FAQ 7) under the limit; notes only.

voice.evidence: Concrete detail ('the upstairs bathroom was missed', 'bank import is the top complaint'); no AI tells.

truth.evidence: FAQ 4's rule 'never send the NPS question to the same customer more than once in 90 days' contradicts tab 3 and its mockup and image, where the survey goes out after each cleaning visit.

distinct.evidence: Own angle (score math, split by plan, low-score email, quarterly trend); no sibling primary in headings; customer feedback survey, customer effort score and customer experience survey appear only as FAQ link anchors; live CSAT page keeps CSAT.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions (AlsoAsked + Semrush questions + secondaries), each answered first; hub link in FAQ 2; 3 sibling links; F9 moat lines in FAQ 7 and 9.

images.evidence: All numbers check: 200+120+80=400, 50%-20%=30; Starter 48/150-30/150=12, Pro 38, Team 55; Teodor Vance 4 to Odalys Ferreira, Friday; Q1 12, Q2 19, Q3 27 on 318 (140-54).

findings.quote: Whatever the rhythm, never send the NPS question to the same customer more than once in 90 days.
findings.issue: The page contradicts itself (CONTENT_DEFECTS #14 class of self-contradiction). FAQ 4 sets an absolute 90-day limit per customer, but the page's own home-services case sends the NPS question after every visit: mockup (homeServices) 'Build an NPS survey for my home cleaning company that goes out after each visit'; tab_content_3 'Saltmarsh Home Cleaning customer Teodor Vance scores his visit a 4'; image_brief tab 3 'Survey sent / After the visit'. A recurring cleaning customer gets the question more often than once in 90 days. FAQ 8 adds to it: 'Right after a single support ticket, ask about that one interaction instead', while tab 3 asks the recommend question about a single visit.
findings.fix: Make one rule hold across the page: either qualify FAQ 4 to relationship surveys (e.g. 'never send the relationship survey to the same customer more than once in 90 days') or change tab 3, its mockup and image so Saltmarsh sends the survey after a customer's first visit, or at most once a quarter per customer. Keep FAQ 8 consistent with the choice.
